headings: Guiding Principles and our Purpose, Vision, and Mission
Environmental Matters and Other Governmental Regulation
paragraphs: We design, manufacture, market and sell professional turf maintenance equipment and services; turf irrigation systems; landscaping equipment and lighting products; snow and ice management products; agricultural irrigation ("ag-irrigation") systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential yard and snow thrower products. Our purpose is to help our customers enrich the beauty, productivity, and sustainability of the land. Our products are marketed and sold worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental centers, and home centers, as well as online and direct to end-users under the primary trademarks of Toro®, Ditch Witch®, eXmark®, Spartan®, BOSS®, Ventrac®, American Augers®, Subsite®, HammerHead®, Radius®, Perrot®, Hayter®, Unique Lighting Systems®, Irritrol®, and Lawn-Boy®, most of which are registered in the United States ("U.S.") and/or in the primary countries outside the U.S. where we market our products branded under such trademarks.

We focus on innovation and quality in our products, customer service, manufacturing, and marketing. We strive to provide innovative, well-built, and dependable products supported by an extensive service network. We commit to funding research, development, and engineering activities in order to improve and enhance existing products and develop new products. Through these efforts, we seek to be responsive to trends that may affect our target markets now and in the future. A significant portion of our net sales has historically been, and we expect will continue to be, attributable to new and enhanced products. We define new products as those introduced in the current and previous two fiscal years.

We have continued to complement our brands, enhance our product portfolios, and improve our technologies through innovation and strategic acquisitions over the more than 100 years we have been in business, including most recently our acquisition of Tornado Infrastructure Equipment Ltd. ("Tornado Infrastructure Equipment"), as discussed below. We plan to continue to leverage a strategic and disciplined approach to pursue targeted acquisitions that add value to TTC by complementing our existing brands, enhancing our product portfolio, and/or improving our technologies. We also plan to continue our commitment to disciplined portfolio management and prudent capital allocation strategies, resulting in our disposition from time to time of non-core product lines.

We classify our operations into two reportable business segments: Professional and Residential. Our remaining activities are presented as "Other" due to their insignificance. These Other activities consist of earnings (loss) from a wholly-owned domestic distribution company, certain corporate activities, and the elimination of intersegment revenues and expenses. Net sales of our reportable segments and Other activities accounted for the following percentages of our consolidated net sales for fiscal 2025: Professional, 80.3 percent; Residential, 19.0 percent; and Other, 0.7 percent.

Sustainability is integrated into our enterprise strategic priorities of accelerating profitable growth, driving productivity and operational excellence, and empowering our people. Our focus on alternative power, smart connected, and autonomous solutions, as well as our continued efforts to address environmental, social, and governance priorities, are embedded as part of our commitment to advancing our sustainability goals.

On December 8, 2025, we acquired Tornado Infrastructure Equipment Ltd., a Calgary, Alberta, Canada-based manufacturer in the hydrovac excavation solutions industry for a purchase price of $279.3 million Canadian dollars. Tornado Infrastructure Equipment manufactures hydrovac excavation solutions and industrial equipment solutions for the underground construction, power transmission, and energy markets and provides innovative product offerings that broaden and strengthen the company's Professional segment and expands its dealer network. The company funded the acquisition with borrowings under its existing revolving credit facility and additional financial arrangements. For additional information regarding the acquisition and the financing agreements utilized to fund the aggregate merger consideration, refer to Note 16, Subsequent Events, in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We strive to be a leader in adapting advanced technologies to products and services that provide innovative solutions for turf maintenance; landscape and lighting; rental, specialty, and underground construction; snow and ice management; agricultural; and residential demands. The following is a summary of our products, by market, for our Professional segment and our products for our Residential segment.

We design professional turf maintenance; landscape and lighting; rental, specialty, and underground construction; snow and ice management; and agricultural products. We market and sell Professional segment products worldwide through a network of distributors and dealers, as well as directly to government customers, rental companies, and large retailers. These channel partners then sell or rent our products to professional and other users, including homeowners, engaged in maintaining turf, such as golf courses, sports fields, municipal properties, as well as residential and commercial landscapes; installing, repairing, and replacing underground pipe and utilities; managing snow and ice demands; irrigating turf and agricultural fields; and creating, renovating, and illuminating landscapes. The following sections describe our Professional segment products by market.

We are the only company to offer both equipment and irrigation products for the golf market and are a market leader in both. We design, manufacture, market, and sell equipment products under the Toro and Ventrac brands that are intended to provide innovative solutions for golf course turf maintenance. Equipment products for the golf market include large reel and rotary riding mowers for fairway, rough, and trim cutting, including autonomous solutions; riding and walking mowers for greens and specialty areas; greens rollers; all-wheel drive articulating tractors; turf sprayer equipment; utility vehicles; aeration equipment; bunker maintenance equipment; other specialty turf equipment; and Intelli360 for telematics and fleet management. We also market and sell irrigation products for the golf market under the Toro brand that are designed to provide innovative water application solutions for golf course turf maintenance. These irrigation products predominantly consist of sprinkler heads, controllers, turf sensors, valves and operating software. These equipment and irrigation products are primarily sold to distributors and dealers, who then sell to owners, managers and/or superintendents of golf courses.

We design, manufacture, market, and sell Toro and Ventrac-branded equipment products that are intended to provide innovative turf maintenance solutions to sports fields and grounds customers. Equipment products for the sports fields and grounds market primarily include riding rotary and reel mowers and attachments, aerators, infield grooming equipment, all-wheel drive articulating tractors, multipurpose vehicles, and versatile debris blowers. In addition to equipment products, we also market and sell irrigation products under the Toro and Perrot brands that are designed to provide innovative water application solutions for sports fields and grounds turf maintenance. These irrigation products primarily include sprinkler heads, controllers, turf sensors, valves and operating software. These products are primarily sold to distributors and dealers, who then sell to owners and/or managers of sports fields, governmental properties, and residential and commercial landscapes, as well as directly to government customers.

We design, manufacture, market, and sell equipment products under the Toro, eXmark, Spartan and Ventrac brands that are intended to provide innovative turf management solutions to landscape contractors. Equipment products for the landscape contractor market include gas and battery powered zero-turn radius riding mowers, heavy-duty and mid-size walk behind mowers including autonomous versions, gas and battery powered stand-on mowers, and manual and remote controlled all-wheel drive articulating tractors, as well as turf application, turf renovation, and tree care equipment. These equipment products are primarily sold to distributors and dealers, who then sell to landscape contractors engaged in turf maintenance activities. These equipment products are primarily sold to distributors and dealers, who then sell to landscape contractors engaged in turf maintenance activities.

We design, manufacture, market, and sell a range of professional grade products to serve the underground construction market under the Ditch Witch, American Augers, HammerHead, Subsite, and Radius brands, including horizontal directional drills, walk and ride trenchers, vacuum excavators, horizontal directional drilling guidance and support equipment, utility locators, utility inspection systems, pipe rehabilitation and replacement solutions, as well as after-market tools, including drive chucks and sub savers, drill pipe, starter rods and quick connects, bits and blades, rock tools, reamers, and swivels. Such products are utilized by specialty contractors worldwide to install water, gas, electric, telecommunication, fiber optic, broadband, and other utility distribution systems.

We design, manufacture, market, and sell Toro and Ditch Witch-branded equipment products that are intended to provide innovative solutions to serve the rental and specialty construction market. These products primarily consist of stand-on skid steers, walk-behind trenchers, stump grinders, and turf renovation products. We also have a line of Toro-branded rental products that feature material handlers and other concrete construction equipment. Our rental and specialty construction equipment products are mainly sold to rental companies and large retailers who subsequently rent the products to end-users, as well as to dealers who market and sell to end-customers primarily consisting of landscape contractors, municipalities, and other government entities.

We design, manufacture, market, and sell equipment products under the BOSS, Ventrac, and Toro brands that are intended to provide innovative snow removal and ice management solutions for the snow and ice management market. These equipment products primarily consist of snowplows; salt and brine ice control products; accessories for light and medium duty trucks, all-terrain vehicles, utility task vehicles, stand-on skid steers, and front-end loaders; and all-wheel drive articulating tractors, sidewalk snow and ice solution vehicles, and related attachments and accessories. These products are mainly sold through distributors and dealers who market and sell to end-customers primarily consisting of landscape contractors, municipalities, and other government entities.

headings: Our net sales and earnings have been and could continue to be adversely affected by economic conditions and outlook in the locations in which we conduct business.
If we are unable to continue to enhance existing products and develop and market new products, demand for our products may decrease.

Our Professional segment includes a variety of products that depend on certain and varied factors.
Changes in product mix could adversely impact our financial performance, including profit margins and net earnings.
We face intense competition, which could harm our business and operating results.
Our domain names are critical assets for informing consumers about our brand, but they are increasingly targeted by scams.
Increases in the cost of commodities, components, parts, and accessories or our other costs of doing business, have, and could continue to, adversely affect our profit margins and businesses.
We are dependent upon the efficient operation of our facilities and those of our suppliers, channel customers, mass retailers, and home centers where our products are sold.
Any failure by us, or our suppliers or channel partners, to hire and/or retain an adequate labor force could adversely affect our business, operating results, and reputation.
Our net sales and/or working capital are negatively impacted when we underestimate or overestimate demand for our products or do not maintain appropriate inventory levels.
Our business and operating results are subject to the inventory management decisions of our channel customers.
Changes in composition of, financial viability of, and the relationships with, our channel customers could negatively impact our business and operating results.
We are dependent upon the availability and terms of credit offered to our customers.
We are dependent upon the effective operation of our information systems, software, or information security practices and those of our business partners or third-party service providers.

Recently announced and future tariffs and other trade restrictions could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following are material risk factors known to us that could materially adversely affect our business, reputation, operating results, industry, financial position, or future financial or operational performance. The risks described below are not the only risks we face. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business, reputation, operating results, industry, financial position, or future financial or operational performance.
This summary is not complete and should be read in conjunction with the more detailed risk factors set forth below.
•Our net sales and earnings have been and will likely continue to be adversely affected by economic conditions and outlook in the locations in which we conduct business.
•If we are unable to enhance existing products and develop and market new products, demand for our products may decrease adversely impacting our net sales and earnings.
•Disruption and/or shortages in commodities, components, parts, or accessories has adversely affected and could continue to adversely affect our business.

•Weather conditions, including conditions exacerbated by global climate change, present chronic and acute physical risks, and have previously impacted, and may continue to impact, demand for some of our products and/or cause disruptions in our operations.

headings: Net Earnings and Net Earnings Per Diluted Share
paragraphs: Our fiscal 2025 results included the following items of significance that are provided in summary format here and described in greater detail throughout the "Results of Operations," "Business Segments," and "Financial Position" sections:
•Consolidated net sales for fiscal 2025 were $4,510.4 million, a decrease of 1.6 percent compared to $4,583.8 million in fiscal 2024.
•Professional segment net sales for fiscal 2025 were $3,624.0 million, an increase of 1.9 percent compared to $3,556.9 million in fiscal 2024.
•Residential segment net sales for fiscal 2025 were $858.4 million, a decrease of 14.0 percent compared to $998.3 million in fiscal 2024.
•Gross margin was 33.4 percent in fiscal 2025, a decrease of 40 basis points compared to 33.8 percent in fiscal 2024.
•Adjusted gross margin was 34.1 percent in fiscal 2025, an increase of 20 basis points compared to 33.9 percent in fiscal 2024.
•SG&A expense as a percentage of net sales in fiscal 2025 was 22.5 percent, an increase of 30 basis points compared to 22.2 percent in fiscal 2024.
•Net earnings for fiscal 2025 were $316.1 million, or $3.17 per diluted share, compared to $418.9 million, or $4.01 per diluted share, in fiscal 2024.
•Adjusted net earnings for fiscal 2025 were $419.6 million, or $4.20 per diluted share, compared to $435.2 million, or $4.17 per diluted share, in fiscal 2024.

•Field inventory was lower as of the end of fiscal 2025 compared to the end of fiscal 2024, primarily due to decreased balances of golf and grounds and turf products, partially offset by higher balances of underground construction products.

•Our order backlog represents unfulfilled customer orders at a point in time. Our order backlog (including shipments beyond 12 months) decreased $0.4 billion to $0.8 billion as of October 31, 2025 from $1.2 billion as of October 31, 2024, primarily driven by improved manufacturing output and more normalized order patterns. Although we continue to see sustained demand for underground construction and golf and grounds products, we expect backlog to normalize by mid-fiscal 2026 given our improved manufacturing output and lower lead times.

We continued our history of paying quarterly cash dividends throughout fiscal 2025 and increased our fiscal 2025 quarterly cash dividend by 5.6 percent to $0.38 per share compared to $0.36 per share paid in fiscal 2024. We also repurchased shares of our common stock under our Board authorized stock repurchase program ("stock repurchase program"), thereby reducing our total shares of common stock outstanding. As a result of the combination of quarterly cash dividends and common stock repurchases, we returned $441.1 million of cash to our shareholders during fiscal 2025. As of October 31, 2025, we had a strong liquidity profile with available liquidity of $1,238.9 million, consisting of cash and cash equivalents of $341.0 million and availability under our revolving credit facility of $897.9 million.

The tariff environment is complex and evolving. Our business has incurred, and expects to continue to incur, additional costs as it relates to tariffs. We have taken and will continue to take action to mitigate inflationary pressures caused by tariffs through a combination of targeted price increases, strategic sourcing adjustments, manufacturing and product portfolio optimization, as well as our ongoing efforts to drive sustainable efficiency gains in our operations and administrative structures.

paragraphs: 我們設計、製造、行銷及銷售專業草坪維護設備與服務；草坪灌溉系統；園藝設備與照明產品；雪與冰管理產品；農業灌溉（"ag-irrigation"）系統；租賃、專業及地下工程設備；以及住宅庭院與雪鏟產品。我們的目標是協助客戶提升土地的美觀、生產力與可持續性。我們的產品透過經銷商、經銷商、量販店、五金零售商、設備租賃中心及居家中心等通路， globally 行銷與銷售，並透過線上及直接對最終用戶銷售，使用 Toro®、Ditch Witch®、eXmark®、Spartan®、BOSS®、Ventrac®、American Augers®、Subsite®、HammerHead®、Radius®、Perrot®、Hayter®、Unique Lighting Systems®、Irritrol® 及 Lawn-Boy® 等主要商標，其中大多已於美國（"U.S.") 及/或於我們行銷這些品牌產品的主要國家註冊。
我們重視產品創新與品質、客戶服務、製造與行銷。我們致力於提供具創新性、品質良好且可靠的產品，並配合廣泛的服務網路。我們承諾投入資金用於研究、開發與工程活動，以改善與提升現有產品並開發新產品。透過這些努力，我們希望能夠回應可能影響我們目標市場的現有與未來趨勢。我們的淨銷售額歷來有相當大一部分，且預期將持續如此，歸因於新產品與增強型產品。我們將新產品定義為在當前及前兩個會計年度所推出之產品。

本公司自營業以來逾100年，持續透過創新與戰略收購來強化品牌、擴充產品組合並提升技術，包括最近收購Tornado Infrastructure Equipment Ltd. ("Tornado Infrastructure Equipment")，如後文所述。本公司計畫持續採用戰略且謹慎的作法，追求能為TTC增加價值的目標收購，以補強現有品牌、擴充產品組合及/或提升技術。本公司亦計畫持續履行謹慎的組合管理與審慎資本配置策略，因此有時會處分非核心產品線。
本公司將營運區分為兩個應報告分部：專業與住宅。其餘活動因規模微小而歸類為"其他"。這些其他活動包含 wholly-owned domestic distribution company 的營業收入（損失）、部分企業活動，以及消除跨分部收入與費用。應報告分部及其他活動的淨銷售額佔本公司合併淨銷售額的百分比，於財務年度2025年為：專業，80.3％；住宅，19.0％；及其他，0.7％。
永續性已納入本公司企業戰略優先事項，即加速獲利成長、提升生產力與營運卓越性，以及賦能員工。本公司對替代能源、智慧連網與自動化解決方案的關注，以及持續努力落實環境、社會與治理（ESG）優先事項，皆已內建於本公司推動永續目標的承諾中。

於2025年12月8日，本公司取得位於加拿大亞伯達省卡爾加里的Tornado Infrastructure Equipment Ltd.公司，該公司為水力真空開挖解決方案產業的製造商，買價為2.793億加元。Tornado Infrastructure Equipment Ltd.製造水力真空開挖解決方案與工業設備解決方案，應用於地下建設、電力傳輸與能源市場，並提供創新產品，以拓展並強化本公司專業分部（Professional segment）的產品線，並擴大其經銷商網路。本公司透過現有循環信用貸款設施的貸款以及額外財務安排來資助此次收購。如需更多關於此次收購及用以資助總合併對價之財務協議的資訊，請參閱本年度10-K表報表第二部分第8項「財務資料與補充資料」所附之會計合併財務報表附註第16項「後續事項」。
本公司致力於成為在將先進科技應用於草坪維護、景觀與照明、租賃、專業與地下建設、雪與冰管理、農業以及住宅需求的產品與服務方面之領導者。以下為本公司專業分部（Professional segment）按市場分類的產品總覽，以及本公司住宅分部（Residential segment）的產品。

本公司設計專業草坪維護、景觀與照明、租賃、專業與地下建設、雪與冰管理以及農業產品。本公司透過經銷商與經銷商網路，以及直接向政府客戶、租賃公司與大型零售商銷售專業分部產品。這些通路夥伴隨後會將本公司產品銷售或出租給專業及其他用戶，包括從事草坪維護的住宅用戶，例如高爾夫球場、體育場地、市政財產，以及住宅與商業景觀；安裝、修復與更換地下管線與設施；管理雪與冰需求；灌溉草坪與農業田地；以及打造、翻新與照明景觀。以下各節說明本公司專業分部產品按市場分類的內容。

本公司為唯一同時提供高爾夫球場用設備與灌溉產品的公司，且在這兩個市場皆為領導品牌。本公司設計、製造、行銷與銷售以 Toro 和 Ventrac 品牌為名的設備產品，這些產品旨在為高爾夫球場草坪維護提供創新解決方案。高爾夫球場用設備產品包括大型旋轉式與滾筒式騎乘割草機，用於球道、粗糙地與修剪區域的切割，包括自動化解決方案；騎乘與步行式割草機，用於球場與特殊區域；球場滾筒；全輪驅動式轉向拖拉機；草坪噴灑設備；多功能車輛；通風設備；沙坑維護設備；其他特殊草坪設備；以及 Intelli360 用於遠端監測與車隊管理。本公司亦行銷與銷售以 Toro 品牌為名的高爾夫球場用灌溉產品，這些產品旨在為高爾夫球場草坪維護提供創新用水解決方案。這些灌溉產品主要為噴頭、控制器、草坪感測器、閥門與操作軟體。這些設備與灌溉產品主要銷售給經銷商與代理商，再由他們銷售給高爾夫球場的擁有者、管理員與/或 superintendent。

本公司設計、製造、行銷與銷售以 Toro 和 Ventrac 品牌為名的設備產品，這些產品旨在為運動場地與園區客戶提供創新草坪維護解決方案。運動場地與園區用設備產品主要包括騎乘式旋轉與滾筒式割草機與配件、通風機、場內維護設備、全輪驅動式轉向拖拉機、多功能車輛與多功能吹除機。除了設備產品外，本公司亦行銷與銷售以 Toro 和 Perrot 品牌為名的灌溉產品，這些產品旨在為運動場地與園區草坪維護提供創新用水解決方案。這些灌溉產品主要包括噴頭、控制器、草坪感測器、閥門與操作軟體。這些產品主要銷售給經銷商與代理商，再由他們銷售給運動場地的擁有者與/或管理員、政府財產、住宅與商業景觀，以及直接銷售給政府客戶。

本公司設計、製造、行銷與銷售以 Toro、eXmark、Spartan 和 Ventrac 品牌為名的設備產品，這些產品旨在為景觀工程承包商提供創新草坪管理解決方案。景觀工程承包商用設備產品包括汽油與電動零轉彎半徑騎乘割草機、重型與中型步行式割草機（包括自動化版本）、汽油與電動站立式割草機，以及手動與遙控全輪驅動式轉向拖拉機，以及草坪應用、草坪翻新與樹木護理設備。這些設備產品主要銷售給經銷商與代理商，再由他們銷售給從事草坪維護工作的景觀工程承包商。

本公司設計、製造、行銷與銷售以 Ditch Witch、American Augers、HammerHead、Subsite 和 Radius 品牌為名的專業級產品，用於服務地下建設市場，包括水平定向鑽機、步行與騎乘式開溝機、真空挖掘機、水平定向鑽機導航與支援設備、電力定位器、電力檢查系統、管道修復與更換解決方案，以及後市場工具，包括驅動夾頭與子保護器、鑽杆、起動桿與快速連接器、刀具與刀片、岩石工具、擴孔器與轉接頭。這些產品被全球專門承包商用於安裝水、氣、電、電信、光纖、寬頻與其他公用設施分佈系統。

本公司設計、製造、行銷與銷售以 Toro 和 Ditch Witch 品牌為名的設備產品，這些產品旨在為租賃與專業建設市場提供創新解決方案。這些產品主要包括站立式拖拉機、步行式開溝機、樹根磨機與草坪翻新產品。本公司亦有以 Toro 品牌為名的租賃產品線，包含物料處理機與其他混凝土建設設備。本公司租賃與專業建設設備產品主要銷售給租賃公司與大型零售商，這些公司隨後將產品租賃給最終用戶，以及銷售給經銷商，這些經銷商行銷與銷售給最終客戶，主要包括景觀工程承包商、地方政府與其他政府機構。

本公司設計、製造、行銷與銷售以 BOSS、Ventrac 和 Toro 品牌為名的設備產品，這些產品旨在為雪與冰管理市場提供創新除雪與冰管理解決方案。這些設備產品主要包括除雪機；鹽與融雪劑冰控制產品；輕型與中型貨車、全地形車、多功能任務車、站立式拖拉機與前裝載機的配件；以及全輪驅動式轉向拖拉機、人行道除雪與冰管理車輛與相關配件與附件。這些產品主要透過經銷商與代理商銷售給最終客戶，主要包括景觀工程承包商、地方政府與其他政府機構。

paragraphs: 本公司財務年度2025之結果包含以下重要項目，以下為簡要格式說明，並於「營運成果」、「業務分部」及「財務狀況」各節有更詳細說明：
•財務年度2025之整體淨銷售額為4,510.4千萬美元，較財務年度2024之4,583.8千萬美元減少1.6％。
•專業業務分部財務年度2025之淨銷售額為3,624.0千萬美元，較財務年度2024之3,556.9千萬美元增加1.9％。
•住宅業務分部財務年度2025之淨銷售額為858.4千萬美元，較財務年度2024之998.3千萬美元減少14.0％。
•財務年度2025之毛利率為33.4％，較財務年度2024之33.8％減少40個基點。
•調整後毛利率為財務年度2025之34.1％，較財務年度2024之33.9％增加20個基點。
•財務年度2025之銷售及一般管理費用佔淨銷售額百分比為22.5％，較財務年度2024之22.2％增加30個基點。
•財務年度2025之淨利為316.1千萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益3.17美元，較財務年度2024之418.9千萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益4.01美元減少。
•調整後淨獲利為財務年度2025年$419.6千萬，即每股稀釋後 shares $4.20，與財務年度2024年的$435.2千萬，即每股稀釋後 shares $4.17相比。
•截至財務年度2025年結束時，現場存貨較財務年度2024年結束時為低，主要由於高爾夫球場與草坪產品餘額減少，部分抵銷地下建設產品餘額增加。
•我們的訂單積壓代表某一時點未履行的客戶訂單。我們的訂單積壓（包括超過12個月的出貨）較2024年10月31日的$1.2千萬減少$0.4千萬至$0.8千萬，主要由於製造產出改善及訂單模式更趨正常化。儘管我們持續觀察到地下建設與高爾夫球場產品的穩定需求，我們預期在財務年度2026年中，積壓情況將趨於正常，這是因為我們製造產出改善且交貨週期縮短。

我們在財務年度2025年持續執行每季現金股息的發放傳統，並將財務年度2025年每季現金股息提高5.6％至每股$0.38，與財務年度2024年發放的每股$0.36相比。我們也根據董事會授權的股票買回計畫（"股票買回計畫"）買回本公司普通股股票，因此減少我們的普通股股票總發行數。由於每季現金股息與普通股買回的結合，我們在財務年度2025年共回饋$441.1千萬現金給股東。截至2025年10月31日，我們擁有強勁的流動性，總可用流動性為$1,238.9千萬，包含現金及現金等價物$341.0千萬，以及循環信貸融資可用額$897.9千萬。
關稅環境複雜且持續變化。我們的業務已產生並預期將持續產生與關稅相關的額外成本。我們已採取並將繼續採取行動，以緩解關稅造成的通貨膨脹壓力，透過針對性價格調漲、戰略採購調整、製造與產品組合優化，以及我們持續推動營運與行政結構永續效率提升的持續努力。

headings: 本公司淨銷售額與獲利已並可能持續受到我們營運所在地區經濟狀況與展望的不利影響。

渠道客戶組成、財務可行性及與本公司之關係變動，可能對本公司業務及營運成果造成負面影響。
本公司依賴客戶所提供之信貸額度及條件。
本公司依賴資訊系統、軟體或資訊安全作業及其商業夥伴或第三方服務提供者之有效運作。
本公司正在整修及擴建部分辦公室、製造及其他設施，可能因相關作業而導致營運中斷。
最近公佈及未來可能實施的關稅及其他貿易限制措施，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
未能順利完成資產處分或其他重整活動，可能對本公司營運造成負面影響。
paragraphs: 下列為本公司所知之重大風險因素，這些因素可能對本公司業務、聲譽、營運結果、產業、財務狀況或未來財務或營運表現造成重大不利影響。下列所述風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。此外，尚有其他未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險，亦可能影響本公司業務、聲譽、營運結果、產業、財務狀況或未來財務或營運表現。
此摘要並非完整，應配合下列更詳細之風險因素一併閱讀。
•本公司之淨銷售額與獲利已受到且將可能持續受到本公司營運所在地區經濟狀況與展望之不利影響。
•若本公司無法改善現有產品並開發與行銷新產品，則本公司產品之需求可能減少，進而對本公司之淨銷售額與獲利造成重大不利影響。
•商品、零組件、零件或配件之供應中斷與/或短缺已對本公司業務造成不利影響，且可能持續造成不利影響。
•天氣狀況，包括因全球氣候變遷而惡化之天氣狀況，會造成慢性與急性之實體風險，且已對部分本公司產品之需求造成影響，或可能持續影響部分本公司產品之需求，並導致本公司營運中斷。
